theory.intro: Many 3D lengths come from a right-angled triangle hidden inside the solid: a diagonal across a face, the slant height of a cone, or the longest rod inside a cylinder. Keep a surd exact unless the question asks you to round.
facts: To find a face diagonal, add the squares of the two edges: $d=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$.
To find a shorter side instead of the hypotenuse, subtract: $a=\sqrt{d^{2}-b^{2}}$.
Leave a surd such as $\sqrt{61}$ for an exact answer; round only when the question asks.
steps: Identify the right-angled triangle and its two known sides.
Decide whether the unknown is the hypotenuse or a shorter side.
Apply Pythagoras' theorem and round only if required.

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular prism has a top face with edges $7\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$. Find the diagonal $d$ across this face. Give an exact answer, then round to $2$ decimal places.
A cone has perpendicular height $7\text{ cm}$ and base radius $3\text{ cm}$. Find its slant height $s$, rounded to $1$ decimal place.
A cylinder has diameter $12\text{ cm}$ and height $17\text{ cm}$. Find the length $L$ of the longest thin straight rod that fits inside it, rounded to $1$ decimal place.
A cone has perpendicular height $10\text{ cm}$ and slant height $14\text{ cm}$. Find its base diameter, rounded to $2$ decimal places.

A cylinder has base radius $4\text{ cm}$. Its longest thin straight rod is $19\text{ cm}$ long, joining opposite points on the two end rims. Find the cylinder's length $l$, rounded to $2$ decimal places.

A pyramid has a rectangular base measuring $8\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$. Its apex $E$ is directly above the centre $O$ of the base. Each apex-to-corner edge is $13\text{ cm}$. Find the perpendicular height $h$, rounded to $1$ decimal place.

development.question_text:
A rectangular prism has a rectangular face with edges $12\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$.
Find the length of the diagonal across this face.
Round to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
The face diagonal $d$ is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with shorter sides $12\text{ cm}$ and $10\text{ cm}$.
$d=\sqrt{12^{2}+10^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{244}$
$\approx15.62\text{ cm}$

development.question_text:
A cone has a base radius of $7\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $16\text{ cm}$.
Find its slant height $s$.
Round to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
The slant height is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with shorter sides the radius and the perpendicular height.
$s=\sqrt{7^{2}+16^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{305}$
$\approx17.5\text{ cm}$

development.question_text:
A cylinder has a base radius of $5\text{ cm}$. A straight rod of length $26\text{ cm}$ reaches from one end to the opposite point on the other end.
Find the length of the cylinder.
Round to $2$ decimal places.
development.solution_text:
First find the diameter: $d=2\times5=10\text{ cm}$.
The rod is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle whose shorter sides are the diameter and the cylinder length $l$.
$l=\sqrt{26^{2}-10^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{576}$
$=24.00\text{ cm}$

development.solution_text:
The face diagonal $d$ is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with shorter sides $13\text{ cm}$ and $18\text{ cm}$.

mastery.question_text:
A rectangular prism has a rectangular face with edges $6.5\text{ cm}$ and $9.2\text{ cm}$.
Find the length of the diagonal across this face.
Round to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
The face diagonal $d$ is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with shorter sides $6.5\text{ cm}$ and $9.2\text{ cm}$.
$d=\sqrt{6.5^{2}+9.2^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{126.89}$
$\approx11.26\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text:
A cone has a perpendicular height of $12\text{ m}$ and a slant height of $15\text{ m}$.
Find its base diameter.
Round to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
The slant height is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle whose shorter sides are the radius $r$ and the perpendicular height.
$r=\sqrt{15^{2}-12^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{81}$
$=9\text{ m}$
The diameter is twice the radius: $d=2\times9=18.00\text{ m}$.

mastery.question_text:
A cylinder has a base radius of $4.5\text{ cm}$. A straight rod of length $15\text{ cm}$ reaches from one end to the opposite point on the other end.
Find the length of the cylinder.
Round to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
First find the diameter: $d=2\times4.5=9\text{ cm}$.
The rod is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle whose shorter sides are the diameter and the cylinder length $l$.
$l=\sqrt{15^{2}-9^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{144}$
$=12.00\text{ cm}$
